title: Good ice cream maker but difficult to assemble and disassemble
text:
Good ice cream maker but difficult to assemble and disassemble. Several years ago my boyfriend purchased a [[ASIN:B0006ONQOC Cuisinart ICE-30BC Pure Indulgence 2-Quart Automatic Frozen Yogurt, Sorbet, and Ice Cream Maker]]. I was so impressed with it that I immediately went out and bought two of them. I wound up giving the extra one I purchased to a friend who also loves it. Therefore, when this T-fal came up for review, I wanted to see how it compared to my Cuisinart.

After using this machine a couple of times, I would have rated this T-fal 3-1/2 to 4 stars had I not already owned the Cuisinart. However, because I am use to such an exceptional ice cream maker, I find this one just okay, so that is why it gets a plain three star-rating from me.

PROS

- It makes one quart of good ice cream (my Cuisinart makes two quarts)

- I made both the strawberry ice cream and the lemon sorbet. The ice cream was good. The lemon sorbet came out excellent; although I was surprised the recipe did not call for heating the egg white. (My Cuisinart recipe uses water instead of egg white.)

- I consider the currently listed price of $34.99 reasonable and it's less than half the price of the Cuisinart I purchased.

- This machine is quieter than my Cuisinart.

CONS

- The ice cream recipes are not exceptional. Although my strawberry ice cream came out good, it was not as creamy or sweet as the recipe that came with my Cuisinart and it tasted icy or more like sorbet. The recipes that came with my Cuisinart are outstanding and a bit more flavorful and probably more calories too. For instance, the T-fal strawberry ice cream recipe calls for strawberries, powdered sugar, lemon, and heavy cream. My Cuisinart recipe also includes adding whole milk and vanilla extract and it uses regular sugar instead of powdered and calls for about ¼ more sugar than the T-fal recipe. I did not mark it down for this because this has nothing to do with the ice cream maker itself and recipe books can always be purchased.

- The chute on the cover is a little too small so it is not as easy to pour in the ingredients without messing up the top.

- Assembling and disassembling the unit is "sticky" and tricky. I had trouble removing the freezer bowl from the base because there is no grip when pulling straight up. Even lining up the top and locking that in place was cumbersome; although after several tries I have that down well. The paddle also requires a good push to get it into the motor but now seats easily.

- The instructions for cleaning are not adequate. There are actually 6 parts to this ice cream maker (as opposed to the 5 parts shown in the instructions). My Cuisinart only has 4 parts. In order to clean everything but the motor, I had to dissemble all parts. Getting the bowl out of the base is the most difficult. However, I had to dissemble the lid after making ice cream because the ice cream got stuck in the crevices of the top. I did not have to do this after the sorbet. The lid coms apart easily as long as I flexed it when I pulled it away from the nubs holding it in place.

- In my opinion, the bowl takes up an odd amount of space in my freezer compared to my Cuisinart. My Cuisinart 2-QT bowl is totally cylindrical and measures 7-3/4 inches wide by 6-3/4 inches tall. This T-fal 1-QT bowl is flared at the top and measures 5-1/2 inches wide at the very bottom to about 9-1/2 wide at the top due to the handles. It also measures 6-1/2 inches tall.

No matter what machine one chooses, making ice cream is messy and requires prior preparation because of the cooking instructions and the fact that time is needed in the freezer for the ice cream to harden. Also making ice cream usually costs more than buying the pre-made product. The joy I get from making my own home-made product, however, far outweighs these caveats.

In summary, although I cannot attest to the longevity of this machine, I think this is a decent ice cream maker for making small quantities of ice cream. Had I not owned a Cuisinart, I would have been more pleased with this machine. However, the cumbersome assembly and disassembly is the main reason it is a three star machine to me.

PS For those who are interested, I pasted a link to my Cuisinart review in the comments section of this evaluation.

product_metadata.title: T-fal IG4000 Ice-Cream Maker, 1-Quart, White
features: Aluminum double wall insulated gel canister
Transparent cover with opening to easily add ingredients
description: Indulge your taste buds with the pure taste of ice cream made in your own home. This T-fal IG400051 ice cream maker is a fun way to make treats for the family. The T-fal ice cream maker helps you to prepare delicious homemade ice cream and frozen treats in minutes. Pour the mixture into the double insulated bowl of the T-fal ice cream maker while in motion. The paddle will automatically churn the mixture into ice cream, frozen yogurt or sorbets without the need for ice. Customize your frozen treats by adding assorted ingredients (candy, cookie bits, nuts, fruit) Enjoy your delicious ice cream or sorbet.
